task_prompt: Invent a two-option decision problem: one certain outcome and one lottery. State at least two outcome probabilities, define a coherent utility for each outcome, calculate both expected utilities and write an answer explaining which option a specified decision maker would select. Make the probabilities total one.
required_output: A self-contained numerical scenario, probability and utility table, correct expected-utility calculation, and justified choice.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Utility weights must apply to outcomes, not be mistaken for monetary averages; probability totals and calculations must be correct.
concept_specific_design_anchor: The choice context is original, alternatives are distinguishable, and the conclusion follows the supplied utilities.
source_citation: von Neumann and Morgenstern, Theory of Games and Economic Behavior (1944), Princeton University Press; expected-utility framework

task_prompt: Design an original experiment that could distinguish a reference-point loss-aversion explanation of an ownership valuation gap from at least one rival explanation. Specify randomization, outcomes, measurements, and a falsifying result.
required_output: A comparison of randomized conditions, operationalized reference states, valuation outcomes, confounds and a falsification criterion.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Distinguish reference-dependent loss aversion from general risk aversion or transaction costs; do not assert a universal loss-to-gain ratio.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Manipulates reference state while keeping object, stakes, and elicitation conditions comparable.
source_citation: Tversky and Kahneman (1991), Loss Aversion in Riskless Choice, https://doi.org/10.2307/2937956

task_prompt: Construct a short randomized study of an irrelevant numeric anchor affecting a factual estimate. Write the exact two prompts, a neutral outcome question, an assignment rule, a pre-specified outcome comparison, and one limitation.
required_output: Two randomized prompts, common estimate question, primary contrast and interpretation limit.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Anchors must be plausibly irrelevant to the quantity and must not themselves carry accurate task information.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Keeps target item and available factual evidence equivalent across treatment arms.
source_citation: Tversky and Kahneman (1974), Judgment under Uncertainty, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124

task_prompt: Write a one-page decision memo for an original project with a past unrecoverable expenditure, two future options, future costs and benefits, and opportunity cost. Create a small numerical table, choose an option and justify the incremental analysis.
required_output: New case, incremental future-value table, decision rule, justified option and one caveat.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Do not include irrecoverable past expenditure in the incremental comparison; include relevant future and recoverable amounts.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Provides two genuinely viable alternatives and makes a numerical or clearly justified qualitative choice.
source_citation: Arkes and Blumer (1985), The Psychology of Sunk Cost, https://doi.org/10.1016/0749-5978(85)90049-4

task_prompt: Compose two mathematically equivalent messages describing one binary-outcome decision: one gain-framed and one loss-framed. Create a randomized evaluation plan, specify an outcome and a safeguard against misleading communication.
required_output: Two equivalent messages, denominator consistency check, randomized contrast and ethical safeguard.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Positive and negative probability/count frames must be exact complements under a shared denominator.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Holds choice outcomes constant and varies only presentation while preserving transparent risk disclosure.
source_citation: Tversky and Kahneman (1981), The Framing of Decisions and the Psychology of Choice, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.7455683

task_prompt: Build an original short diagnostic exercise with three distinct mini-scenarios designed to elicit availability, representativeness and anchoring. For each, specify the expected error, a discriminating follow-up question and one alternative explanation.
required_output: Three novel mini-scenarios, mapped heuristic hypotheses, counterchecks and confounds.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Distinguish recall accessibility, resemblance-to-prototype, and starting-number effects; avoid defining all errors as the same bias.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Each vignette targets a distinct cue and supplies a testable alternative explanation.
source_citation: Tversky and Kahneman (1974), Judgment under Uncertainty, https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124

task_prompt: Create a pair of original choices that hold final monetary outcomes constant while changing the stated reference point. Predict, under an explicitly named prospect-theory assumption, how valuation could differ, and design a comparison that might falsify your prediction.
required_output: Paired choice descriptions, explicit reference points, model assumptions, prediction and testable counterexample.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Separate gains/losses from final wealth, and distinguish reference dependence from probability-weighting assumptions.
concept_specific_design_anchor: The paired alternatives are objectively comparable while changing an interpretable reference point.
source_citation: Kahneman and Tversky (1979), Prospect Theory, https://doi.org/10.2307/1914185

task_prompt: Design an original, ethically defensible default or reminder intervention to help people make an informed choice. Draw or describe the complete choice interface, opt-out, evaluation outcome, randomization and adverse-effect monitoring plan.
required_output: Original choice architecture, documented opt-out, randomized evaluation design and monitoring criteria.
concept_specific_accuracy_anchor: Preserves meaningful freedom of choice, recognizes transparency and possible welfare tradeoffs; does not equate click rate with benefit.
concept_specific_design_anchor: Includes a usable, reversible choice interface and both benefit and unintended-consequence measures.
source_citation: Thaler and Sunstein (2008), Nudge: Improving Decisions About Health, Wealth, and Happiness, Yale University Press, ISBN 9780300122237
